facility_roles.quote: Belle II is an intensity-frontier experiment at the SuperKEKB collider in Tsukuba, Japan.

intervals.label: proposal
intervals.note: End of the interval is the publication of the Technical Design Report (arXiv:1011.0352, 1 November 2010).

intervals.label: design and construction (TDR to roll-in)
intervals.note: Start: the Belle II Technical Design Report, submitted 1 November 2010, which states 'A new international collaboration Belle-II, is being formed.' End: the roll-in of the assembled detector to the SuperKEKB interaction point.
intervals.quote: On 11 April, the Belle II detector was successfully “rolled-in” to the collision point

intervals.label: Phase 2 (pilot run)
intervals.note: INSPIRE gives date_started 26 April 2018 for the experiment. Phase 2 ran without the full vertex detector.
intervals.quote: the first collisions recorded in the early hours of April 26th

intervals.label: Phase 3 / Run 1 physics data taking
intervals.note: KEK press release of 11 March 2019: Belle II 'now fully equipped and ready to take physics data'. Run 1 ended with the start of Long Shutdown 1, which KEK IPNS dates only to 'the summer of 2022'.
intervals.quote: Phase 3 operation of the SuperKEKB project began successfully

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 1
intervals.note: A new two-layer pixel vertex detector and an improved beam pipe were installed.
intervals.quote: The accelerator and detector were both upgraded during a long-shutdown that started in the summer of 2022

intervals.label: Run 2
intervals.note: The collider itself restarted on 29 January 2024; this interval starts at the first recorded Run 2 collisions.
intervals.quote: At 22:12 JST on the 20th of February, the Belle II detector recorded the first electron-positron collisions

quantity.quote: The beam energies for the High Energy Ring (HER) and the Low Energy Ring (LER) are 7 GeV and 4 GeV, respectively

quantity.note: As stated on belle2.org on 2026-09-16. The March 2025 Belle II strategy input quoted 'about 575 fb⁻¹'.
quantity.quote: we have accumulated a total of 914 fb-1 of data rich in beauty and charm hadrons as well as tau leptons

quantity.note: The Belle II Physics Book states the same target: 'It is anticipated to collect 50/ab of collision data over its lifetime.'
quantity.quote: Our goal is to accumulate an integrated luminosity of 50 ab–1 by the mid of next decade

lineage.quote: To exploit the increased luminosity, an upgrade of the Belle detector has been proposed. A new international collaboration Belle-II, is being formed.

name: Belle II
notes: facility:kek is owned by the japan-neutrino workstream and is referenced only.

physics_goals.note: Third goal from the Belle II strategy input: 'searches for new physics beyond the SM across flavor, tau, electroweak, and dark sector physics'.
physics_goals.quote: The experiment's low-background environment and precisely known kinematics enable high-precision measurements of hundreds of Standard Model (SM) parameters while probing for new particles at mass scales far beyond the direct reach of high-energy colliders.
value: Search for physics beyond the Standard Model in the decays of B mesons, charm hadrons and tau leptons
Make high-precision measurements of Standard Model flavour parameters
Search for dark-sector particles and other new light states

summary.plain: The successor to the Belle experiment at the KEK laboratory in Japan. Running since 2019, it records electron-positron collisions from the SuperKEKB machine, looking for tiny departures from the known laws of physics in the decays of heavy, short-lived particles.
summary.technical: Intensity-frontier e⁺e⁻ experiment at SuperKEKB (√s = 10.579 GeV), aiming at 50 ab⁻¹ to probe flavour observables in B, charm and tau decays and to search for dark-sector states; 914 fb⁻¹ recorded by September 2026.

unique_capabilities.note: Third item derived from the recorded and target integrated luminosities.
unique_capabilities.quote: The experiment's low-background environment and precisely known kinematics enable high-precision measurements
value: Reconstruction of decays with neutrinos or photons using the precisely known e⁺e⁻ initial state
A low-background environment compared with hadron colliders
The world's largest e⁺e⁻ data set at the Υ(4S) resonance
